long_biography.plain_text:
Abraham Cababie Daniel began by arranging international franchise agreements for his family's textile enterprise. Mexico's trade liberalisation altered that industry's prospects, and in 1989 he joined brothers Elías and Jacobo in moving into property development. Their new business became GICSA.

Cababie took the chief-executive role while Elías chaired the board, a division of responsibility that continues. GICSA expanded across shopping centres, offices, mixed-use complexes, industrial space, housing and hospitality before listing shares publicly. Abraham also serves as board vice-chairman. The Cababie Daniel family and related parties held 57.27 per cent of the company in 2024. No individual percentage was allocated to Abraham. His co-founding, executive work and family ownership support real estate as both the source and current focus of his wealth. GICSA's properties, investment budgets, debt and market value remain corporate measures rather than his personal assets.

Abraham Cababie Daniel is GICSA's chief executive and vice-chairman. His brother Elías Cababie Daniel is executive chairman. Their roles are separately stated and Elías's chairmanship is not attributed to Abraham.

The 2024 annual report groups the Cababie Daniel family and related parties at 57.27 per cent of GICSA. It does not allocate Abraham's individual direct or indirect holding, so neither the complete family block nor sole control is assigned to him.

Abraham, Elías and Jacobo jointly established the GICSA business after a family textile career. Abraham is therefore described as a co-founder, not the sole founder; the other brothers' work and interests are not attributed to him.

The family textile company provided commercial experience, relationships and security before the move into property. Self-made — advantaged start reflects that platform while recognising that the brothers built the principal real-estate asset rather than inheriting an already completed GICSA business.

GICSA's property portfolio, development area, investment budgets, construction expenditure, project values, debt, revenue and market capitalisation belong to the listed company. They are not treated as Abraham Cababie's personal assets or net worth.
